While not my usual taste in games, this game has a lot of subtle ideas. For those of you considering playing, please don't read any further.
This game deals with the question of homosexuality, and acceptance, as we learn through the story. Whether the parents ever accepted their daughter (the protaganist's younger sister), is unknown (I personally believe not, based on the amount of biblical literature you see, and the evidence of a slowly disintigrating marriage). While it is a love story, it focuses on a young girl's self-doubts, and self-realization of her love for another woman, and it tells it in a very quiet, story-driven manner. While the creators, without a doubt, could've done something far more action-packed with their time and efforts, they chose to do a game like this, when there are a lot of peole struggling with the question of self-identity & sexual identity.
That said, it could've been more interesting (sub-plot with the ghost, if there was one, was a little unresolved feeling).
For those of you who had a tl;dr: Good game, needed for people struggling with understanding homosexuality or their own sexuality. Has some parts that could be improved, but not much.

This game is skill based not weapon based, I had to restart at level 1 with rookie gear, items, yadayada, I was thrown into a match with a level 50, 35, and another lvl 1, I came in first. I had 10 kills more than the lvl 50, he had nice gear and was even premium, but becasue I pulled the trigger faster, I out did him, your skills matter, not your gear, though nice gear DOES help, like, better armour, better scopes, underbarrel attachments and barrel attachments, which can all be swapped out WHILE in the battlefield, the classes are balanced, and as long as you can aim you can get the kill, with any gun, Hackers exist, you can't escape them, they are in every corner of the internet, but there isn't than many in all honesty,
Pros: Balanced Classes, Skill based fighting always trumps Pay to Win, you can have the GREATEST gun in the entire game, and still get killed by the level 2 with a pistol, if you can shoot, you can get the kill. FREE Item progression, you can unlock items from 3 catagories as you play the game, which is really nice, you don't need to toss cash in to be able to get better armour or weapon attachments, just earn it, yes paying will help out, but only in an aesthetic in all honesty.
Cons: If you're good, you're good, if you're bad.. You're Dead.
Some of the most veteran players have learned little tricks to aid themselves, a lot of the time, if you ahve a healer on your team (in PVE Combat) they will run forward with their shotgun, ahead of everyone else, and tank all hte kills, using their medic bag to only heal themselves, and ditch the other players behind, taking not only all the kills, but letting the entire team drag in the dust, a lot of snipers are good at aiming and (I admit I've done it) run through shooting any enemy they see either in the head or chest and taking all of the kills before you can even aim, becasue of the range they can have at their benefit, with minimal damage to themselves.
Over all, fun game, good community and from what I've seen, a lot of updates and events to keep things interesting. Reccomended

Moderately fond of this game. I don't think it's either the amazing game of the year that so many reviews painted it as or the pile of garbage that so many gamers like to think it is. Just to be totally clear, if you're the kind of person who hates games that focus on story to the detriment of gameplay, just don't even bother. The gameplay consists of walking around and solving some very simple puzzles. Really just figuring out where to go next is the only challenge and it's not that hard.
The good: The story was generally pretty engaging and it's kind of a new issue for games to be tackling
. The eerie atmosphere of the house is great too. I liked how things came together at the end to show why the house is deserted too. The subplot involving the martial problems of the parents was pretty interesting too, moreso than the main plot for me.
The bad: While the story is told in a fairly new and interesting way, the story itself just isn't that interesting. The main plot follows
Also, while telling the story through diary entries was definitely engaging, it does feel kind of contrived having them all just lying around and telling such a complete story.
But still, overall I'd say give it a go if you're not bothered by gameplay-lite games. It's not revolutionary and it's pretty rough but it's still different as far as games go and it only takes about 2 hours of your time.
Actually, on that note, the dev is having a laugh pricing this at €20 for the game. This is absolutely not worth that much. I think I got it on a sale for €5 and that was a fair enough price but this is literally the length of an average film, just a lot more slow-paced and coming in at twice the price, so I really couldn't recommend buying it at RRP. Get it in a Humble Bundle or a sale.

I see a lot of negative reviews, but the only grounds given is the dlc-mess.
Sure, FROM did some mistakes with the dlc's (promising there would be none, pricing, etc), but the game itself does not suffer from this, only your wallet and/or trust in FROM.
As for the game itself, the combat feels fluid, the environments are pretty, and the feeling of finally beating that one boss after a hundred tries is the best ever. I love the gameplay, and the graphics are pretty good as well.
There are lots of viable builds that you will discover as you play the game. I have put all my play time into my knight, but I have read a lot on reddit about pve/pvp meta, and it seems to confirm that there is no "strongest" option.
There is a point about the gameplay that is negative. The game gives you very little information about available options. You kill a boss and pick up it's soul. You see that you can consume it for a large amount of souls, but in the beginning there is no way of knowing that you can get weapons/armor from it later in the game, leading to a lot of regret.
A lot of people on reddit seem to say that the first playthrough is the most fun because you learn to overcome greater and greater challenges on your own, while others would say the later playthroughs. This is due to overcoming the skill requirement and allowing you to do fun things like no block/parry runs and fashion souls (look it up). I cannot speak for either option though, as i have yet to complete my first. Still one of my favorite games so far.
Would reccomend to anyone who
- Enjoys a challenge and does not quit easily
- Does not tie the quality of a game to outside factors (See 1st paragraph)
- Likes a wide array of customization options
- Loves the feeling of mastery after FINALLY beating something they've struggled with for hours.

I have a thumbs down review because, at the end of the day, the time I put into it ultimately didn't feel nearly as rewarding as it was in other games I've played. Honestly, I wish they had a score between thumbs up and thumbs down. This is by no means a bad game, but it's not one that I can recommend among other games I have played.
This game is always super cheap, and it is easily worth the three bucks I paid for it. That said, while it was worth every penny, it wasn't worth every hour. The gameplay is solid and engaging, but once you've played 2 hours you've seen everything this game has to offer. Also, I'm not a fan of the idea that to "claim" an area, you are basically doing a collectible hunt.
EDIT: For the record: "collectible hunt" doesn't just mean picking things up. There are also fuel tanks, radio towers, etc. However, I argue strongly that there is only a semantic difference between picking up a box or blowing up one of 3 different types of destructible object buried in corners of an area. It's still effectively a collectible hunt.
The game is an open-world third person shooter that has limited sandbox elements. Most of the game you spend generating "Chaos" in order to unlock the next mission in either the main story-arc or the next mission in your faction. Unfortunately, causing "chaos" generally means "find the collectibles in uninteresting and repetive towns." This is really where I got bored with the game super quickly. You spend more time just walking around areas staring at your proximity indicator to find collectibles than you will even come close to spending on missions. Honestly, the mission themselves can be enjoyable, but it's overshadowed by the simply silly amounts of "collectible grinding" you have to do to unlock them.
Simply put, grinding "chaos" points is where this game falls flat. It encourages you to spend inordinate amounts of time just walking around an area looking for the one or two collectibles/fuel tanks you missed without actually doing interesting missions.
Above all else, let me be clear. This game is NOT GTA on steroids. The only thing it has in common with GTA is an open-world, a third person camera, and the existence of cars and guns. That's it. It is a very different game.
GOOD
-Surprisingly good gunplay for a third person open world shooter without a lock-on mechanic
-Beautiful, vast world with diverse scenery
-Long game with a lot of gameplay
-Fantastic DPH (dollars per hour) entertainment value
BAD
-Collectible hunting is fine for side missions, but this game requires you spent the vast majority of your time hunting collectibles.
-Lack of depth; This game has amazing breadth, but incredibly little depth. There just simply isn't a whole lot of depth.
-Once you've played 3 hours, you've seen everything except the scenery.
-I lost interest in the story so fast I honestly forgot about it almost entirely.
-Too much time is spent just travelling between areas without seeing anything interesting. The towns themselves get very repetitive.
-Awkard control schemes at times.
-Heat (wanted level) system is far more annoying than it is fun or challenging.
-Ammo is expensive to buy, hard to find.
Is Just Cause 2 a bad game? No, of course not.
But if you're like me and have a working backlog of Steam Games to get to, I'd say this one is low priority. That said, the game has aged well, and will certainly have you entertained for a few hours even if you don't play too much into it. That can easily be worth the periodic super cheap price.

A beautiful story-game - a must-buy if on sale.
Like Dear Esther, Gone Home takes the player on a dual-journey as both the protagonist you play (Katie); returning home and piecing together family chemistry, and occasionally punctuating this with audio-diaries of your sister's (Sam) journey of self-discovery.
Every member of the family has their own interests and troubles, and there are clear cross-overs and "favourites" between the family members. Although sometimes cliché, it's also heart-warming thanks to the excellent voice acting and "breadcrumb" style of writing within the game.
The game balances the seriousness of harsh reality, which on occasion brought a smile to my face and a tear to my eye, with the silliness of children and as I played I was reminded of mid-1990 to early 2000 films of American Teens finding their place in the world as Gone Home fits squarely within this genre in my opinion; complete with terrible angsty girl-band vocals!

I must admit that I've been pleasantly surprised by Warface.
I was expecting the kind run of the mill, pay to win experience that a lot of free to play shooters offer, but so far I've been very satisfied with the experience. The game offers straight-forward, competitive gunplay which rewards players that have more skill more than it rewards players that have more cash on hand. It's simple enough and for the most part is pretty entertaining. Co-op missions are also a good time, with a fair amount of variety and a good balance between challenge and accesibility.
The thing that has struck me more than anything is the communisty itself. In my eight hours of play so far (and I do understand that's not so much, but it's enough to get a feel for the game) I haven't yet had a negative experience with another player. Being matched with strangers in a lobby I've been able to get along wiht everybody just fine and complete missions, which definitely reqard teamwork without forcing it on to the player.
Maybe I'm too new to offer an in-depth review, but so far I have no major complaints. Warface is a solid pick if you want a shooter to kill a few hours with.

I can't believe I waited this long to play Gone Home.  Sure, I completed it in one evening with some time to spare, but the story has really stuck in my head since.  The atmosphere is fantastic -- the house is incredibly spooky and the story behind the house was incredibly intriguing and made even creepier by the rain/thunder/darkness.  I was completely enthralled with this game from beginning to end.  Don't forget to play all of the tapes you find around, especially the Heavens to Betsy casettes (Corin Tucker of Sleater-Kinney fame's band from early/mid 1990s).
I'm glad to see how much hype Gone Home has received -- it's well worth it and I hope they continue to make games like this.  There's so much going on in just a couple hours worth of gameplay, but it comes together so well without forcing every problem to have a solution (much like real life!).  Having a strong female AND LGBT lead is such a big deal, I really applaud Fullbright for everything they've done here.

If you are looking for a game that is PURE fun, then this is the game you want to get. This game will provide you with a huge variety of weapons, land/water/air vehicles and a enormous, gorgeous outdoor map to wreak chaos, havoc and mayhem.
It feels as a very refreshing experience in a way that it eliminates all restrictions and linearity you will find in other games, even surpassing the freedom in GTA while still guiding you enough to not feel without purpose or goal.
The game has a cheesy storyline, fortunatly the cutscenes can be skipped and wont distract you from your gameplay. You wont be missing out on content since blackmarket weapons and vehicles are unlocked via the Chaos you create by wreaking havoc and mayhem. Weapons and vehicles can also be upgraded to increase things like ammo capacity, damage, speed, handling, etc. by collecting crates scattered across Panau. You choose for yourself which weapons and vehicles you want to upgrade. Blackmarket weapons and vehicles can be called from anywhere using a beacon after which a helicopter will drop your purchase in front of you.
DLC-wise it is up to you. The weapons and vehicles are fun to use and are available and upgraded to the max from the start, but you don't need the DLC to have a good experience.
The only thing I wont recommend getting is the "Just Cause Collection". You are better off getting Just Cause 2 and the DLC seperatly. The original "Just Cause" is a very old game and "Just Cause 2" is just better in every way in my opinion.
This concludes my review about Just Cause 2, I hope that you'll find this helpfull in making your decision.

What can I say? One of a kind !
If you've been longing for a good WW1 shooter. Or If you just like shooters, this game will get you hooked.
You will need patience and practise though because this game is hard. It's brutal reality; one shot will kill you.
And you will die ALOT !
But it captures the fighting in the trenches like no other game ever has.
Storm the enemy trench across No-man's land with your buddies and see them wiped out by machine gun fire.
Crawl out off the crater you've been cowering in and get your head blown off by a sharpshooter.
Even staying in the trench isn't safe as artillery fire and poison gas will force you out of hiding.
But the feeling you get the first time you strike down an unsuspecting foe with a high powered bolt-action rifle makes all the hardships worthwhile.
Further adding to the authenticity you will find that each of the authentic weapons, apart from being beautifuly modelled and textured has a unique feel to it and you will quickly develop preferences
BTW: This already great game just recently got updated with a ton of new features, uniforms, factions and weaponry.
My conclusion: The price is right, Buy it !

This game is super disappointing.  I bought it recently hoping for another Red Orchestra 2 experience, but frankly found a broken game.  It runs like molasses, and I barely get over 45 FPS (considering Just Cause 3 runs perfectly with ultra, this is inexcusable) with terrible latency and server lag (I never have over 30 ping, but the game still lags like crazy).  The game itself has tremendous potential, but it falls flat on it's face.  Weapon balance is terrible, team balance is even worse, and the game just decides not to work sometimes.  In many cases, if you join in a game you won't be able to spawn at all, meaning you'll have to leave, rejoin, and try again.  This isn't a problem on my end, it seems to be a really common problem.
-REVISION: If you slaughter the options menu down to potato levels, you can actually get 60fps when staring at a wall, however, it still drops significantly whenever smoke or a couple of other players are on the screen
This game is also one of those multiplayer games that choose "realism" over balanced gameplay.  Many weapons are just blatantly better than others: why would you choose to use a bolt-action rifle, when their is a fully-automatic BAR to choose, which does the same damage, has no recoil, and dishes out 20 round magazines at 500 RPM?
-ADDITION: this is actually even worse now.  You pretty much either join the allied side (with the BAR and RSC 17 etc) or you lose, that's pretty much it.  Teams end up with the Allied sides having 14+ players to the Central power's 8 or even less, making for one-sided gameplay.  The "autobalance" of teams is the worst I've ever seen in games, it never actually switches anyone, it just "suggests" you to switch.  If nobody switches it takes points from you, but considering the points it takes are less than what you get for just killing one person, there is no point.
I love the feel of the game, and the premise is very cool, but the actual gameplay is frankly disappointing.  It's not uncommon to end up in a match where your team has 10 people and the enemy team has a full roster, each one toting an SMG or a machine gun.  This doesn't even go into the constant artillery and grenade spam, considering one class gets up to 5 grenades, and another can call in mortar strikes, which can kill you through walls and behind rocks.
-ADDITION: the class balance between nations is broken too.  Some nations get to have a rifle and some grenades, some get a pistol and grenades, and some get...a melee weapon and grenades...why on earth would you choose a melee weapon, instead of a rifle or pistol?
In terms of polish, this game is very buggy, with many weapons having misaligned iron sights (pretty important to get right you know?) this is especially bad on the MGs, with several being inconsistantly off, sometimes shooting to the left, sometimes to the right, and other times high and low. There are also problems with collision boxes of terrain, and many other minor things
-ADDITION: maps are very hit-or-miss too, some of them blatantly favoring one side or the other.  For instance one map in particular is LITERALLY an up-hill fight for one side, and I've never seen them win, or even draw on that map.  However other maps are really enjoyable, getting some very awesome situations.

I've already reviewed Dark Souls II - the summary being that I didn't recommend it, but mostly because I think it's a very unpredictable thing if someone will get a kick out of frustration and failure. Not a bad game, just not something that everyone's going to like. A lore that's only hinted at in bits and some unfortunate graphics in spots only heighten this uncertainty.
However, SotFS edition I'm just going to not recommend at all.
It doesn't do much with 64-bits? Possibly the wider register will help with some mid-powered systems but for some reason the minimum requirements have jumped up a bit. Strange since the 'updated graphics' are virtually non-existent. There are plenty of comparison shots online to browse and maybe for some people it will be compelling but it seems to be little more than a different graphical filter. By no means did they overhaul their textures, so don't expect your graphics card to be getting more of a workout.
The game balance has been ruined in favour of expanded multiplayer. This is probably a criticism that not everyone is going to agree with - I'm sure there are plenty who think it's still not hard enough. Or there are those whose sole retort will be 'get good', and bravo on their wit. But, where the difficulty had previously felt correct for the experience, there are now many places that feel like you're being strong-armed into summoning others. This new scaling has resulted in single player feeling untenable in places and, should you get 5 or 6 people together, pretty much make any encounter a joke.
Finally, they've altered the location of enemies. This might be a somewhat petty complaint but they didn't just move enemy type A from location X to Z. They didn't just give A a couple of friends. They replaced enemy A with enemy E which, as far as I can tell, shouldn't be there according to the bits of lore I've seen. Sure, maybe I missed something. Maybe they just wander freely and have a movie night or something, but it feels like they're just ignoring what they want in the name of changing it up a little to justify a price tag that shouldn't have been set so high.

I don't think I can recommend this game enough for anybody looking to have a blast. As a person who typically doesn't like open-world games, I have to admit that I spend way more time on this game than I thought I would.
I bought Just Cause 2 at a sale, when it was about €2 euro's. Although i heard great things about it, I didn't know if it was gonna be any good. Within the first twenty minutes, I wasn't very impressed. The game tried to invest me in the story by dumping a hugh amount of exposition on me to no avail. It simply reminded me of 80's action movies where the story plays second fiddle to the action and is just there to give you an excuse to turn your brain off.
The 80's action movie vibe continued, and increased the more you play. Turns out that you are an agent send to overthrow the dictator of a fictional Oceanic country, and the way to go about your business is to blow EVERYTHING up to reduce the influence of said dictator. Oilfields, military bases, water towers and lot's more things that go boom are there for you to destroy at your own leisure. While there are MANY side missions you can complete, you can only continue the main story line if you have blown enough places to smithereens. The game gives you a great variety of weapons, cars, planes and boats to do so, and thankfully the handling of those items or vehicles is equally forgiving and unrealistic as the story, and I wouldn't have want it any other way. Did I also mention you have an infinite supply of grappling hooks and parachutes which you can use to create the most impossible of stunts? The game promotes experimenting with these tools and more often than not, creates satisfying results
I could go on and on about how utterly rediculous this game is. The end of the game has you fighting the final boss while riding mid-air nukes trying to prevent World War 3. It's things like these that make it a real shame that this game hardly gets any exposure. It truly is one of the most fun games I've played in a long time, certainly at the low price i paid for it. If you're looking for a game that is provoking you to blow up as much as you can in a world that has NO boundaries, look no further.

Review: Counter-Strike: Source is a late predecessor of current generation First Person Shooters that has adopted and retained mechanics that are reminiscent of its former titles in the series. The level of skill required to master the game is in most aspects to a higher difficulty than that of other FPS games. Accompanying the base game, community made modifications including maps, skins or game modes can be found in the server browser. Unlike other common games however, Counter-Strike does not award players constantly with rewards or achievements nor does it have a leveling system. For a game made 10 years ago, the quality in development and execution is tremendous. These characteristics are reverberated throughout each of the Counter-Strike games and thus makes it one of my most favourite series of all.

A quintessence of good and bad in japaneese console gaming. Invincibility frames don't belong in a slasher and removing 'press X to not get hit' prompts so player has to learn timings himself doesn't make gameplay feel less of a QTE sequence.
While if did hook me up with that good old MetroidVania action+exploration theme filled with lore and tons of different loot to find and use, it's core gameplay mechanics suck utterly hard. Why bother programming a good AI that is both fun and challenging to fight? Give NPC enemies unlimited stamina so they can spam attacks, give their attacks player movement tracking mid-animation so they can hit a player that is standing behind them with a forward slash and give the player an unlimited supply of healing items to cope with that, yay.
The most disappointing part was the swordplay. Having 300 different weapons is neat, but not when it's quantity over quality. Many hitboxes are buggy and overall balance is poor. At first I was excited, but it turned out that there is a pool of 20-30 moves per weapon type and every sword of spear uses only 8-10 out of them. So instead of having a weapon with a bunch of parameters like damage/length/etc and a rich pool of moves that is the same for all same weapons we have 8 swords with predefined move sets. One can do an uppercut, but cannot do a forward piercing attack. An awful game design choice.
1. Make sets of moves and call it 'stances'
2. More complex/strong stances require more STR or DEX to use depending on given weapon requirements.
3. Every weapon can use every move there is in the game (except for magical special attacks).
4. Problem solved.
TL;DR Plethora of bad game design choices killed a potentially very good game.

Open-world action game as it should be.
has that great feeling of absolute freedom - go anywhere, drive anywhere, fly anywhere! You can get to any place on the huge map in just few seconds, you can be defeated without any penalties - this game is here to entertain you, not to blow your mind or make you angry at your keyboard.
Two unique devices underlying the awesomeness of
are grappling hook and infinitely respawning parachute (infinitely resp...? aw, forget it). Tons of fun guaranteed! Every action game should have it - I really missed them in
. ;-) It brings so much variety and joy in moving and fighting that you'll be travelling for hours here and there just to use them again and again.
The world is really good. Yes, most of the cities and villages are copy-pasted, but there are so many different regions on the map with different climate, weather and views that you'll never get bored. Graphics is on the level too, especially fire and explosions - you'll get addicted to blowing things up! Story and quests are not the strongest part of the game, but they do their job. Another feature worth mentioning is the hidden items' search radar - in my opinion, really great idea. It is finally interesting to find stuff by yourself without spending hours in vain or using guide from the Internet.
There are some cons, of course. Enemies respawning out of nowhere behind your back can be really annoying sometimes. Weapon arsenal is not so big, besides, the lack of ammunition for some weapons leaves you with even less choices. Main story is very short and optional quest lines are not so long either. But there are many things to do on the map - different challenges, races, liquidation contracts... Finally, there's still (and I guess it will be there forever) a bug that prevents you from getting the cherished 100% completion of the game (by the game's internal statistics, not the Steam's one). Thankfully there's only achievement for 75% completion, so no worries, achievement hunters - you'll get your perfect Steam game. ;-)
If you like free roaming in beautiful open-world game, spending time in parachute challenges, races and outpost fightings, searching for hundreds of collectibles and upgrades, spreading chaos by blowing stuff up or just flying around and enjoing you freedom - you'll definitely love
.
------------------------------
Экшн с открытым миром - такой, каким он должен быть.
дарит чувство абсолютной свободы - иди куда хочешь, рули куда хочешь, лети куда заблагорассудится. В любую точку огромной карты можно добраться за секунды, никаких штрафов за гибель героя - эта игра призвана развлекать вас, а не взрывать мозг или доводить до бешенства.
Два уникальных девайса, делающих игру такой шикарной - гарпун и бесконечно восстанавливающийся парашют (бесконечно восстан...? а, неважно). Веселье гарантировано! Эти штуки должны быть в каждом экшене - как мне не доставало их в
!.. ;-) Простое перемещение по миру и заурядные перестрелки становятся настолько разнообразней и веселей, что вы будете путешествовать туда-сюда только для того, чтобы снова воспользоваться ими.
Мир игры по-настоящему хорош. Да, большая часть городков и деревень сделана копи-пастом. Но на карте столько разных мест со своим климатом, погодой, видами вокруг, что скучно не будет. Графика тоже на уровне, особенно огонь и взрывы - вы полюбите разносить всё в щепки! Сюжет и побочные квесты не сильная сторона игры, но своё дело они делают. Отдельного упоминания стоит система поиска скрытых предметов с помощью радара - на мой взгляд, отличное решение! В кои-то веки интересно искать ценные предметы самому, а не бегать часами там, где ничего нет, или сверяться с готовой картой из Инета.
Конечно, есть некоторые минусы. Враги, респавнящиеся из ниоткуда прямо за спиной, порой жутко раздражают. Арсенал не так уж велик, а нехватка патронов для некоторых пушек ещё сильнее ограничивает в выборе. Основная сюжетная линия очень коротка, да и дополнительные квесты проходятся быстро. Тем не менее, заняться есть чем - всяких испытаний, гонок и контрактов на устранение на карте хватает. Наконец, достичь заветного 100%-го прохождения игры (игра ведёт свою внутреннюю статистику, не связаную со Steam) не получится из-за бага, который, очевидно, никто уже не исправит. К счастью, Steam-достижение есть только за 75%-ое прохождение, так что будьте спокойны, охотники за ачивами - вы сможете получить в коллекцию ещё одну "идеальную" игру. ;-)
Если вам нравится рассекать по открытому красивому миру, проводить время за парашютными испытаниями, гонками и сражениями за военные базы, искать сотни спрятанных предметов и апгрейдов, сеять хаос, взрывая всё вокруг, или просто летать, наслаждаясь видом и собственной свободой, вам определённо понравится
.

-Beautiful and deadly-
A must-buy for action-RPG fans who aren't afraid of dying or easily frustrated.
Not quiet as unforgiving as DS1, DS2 is still pretty brutal with a large world, multiple paths to victory and a lonely melancholic feeling.
There's no hand-holding here, traps are set to kill you, other players will invade to also kill you and if you walk into a deep chasm you'll be dead. Same goes for the towering boss monsters and the famous "heavily armored knights on roller blades".
You can take only a few hits, restoring health costs a moment to use, blocking, dodging and attacking uses stamina - the fights are intense and probably the best melee in gaming.
The athmosphere is spot on from the beautiful graphics to voice acting and music, the sad dying world is perfectly captured. Unlike DS1 the sense of place and moving through enemy ground is diminished because of early waypoint teleporting  you won't get lost easily or stuck in a deep dungeon.
A hub town offers a safe shelter similar to the firelink shrine in the first DS.
Hints visible in online play where other players tell you of ambushes and secrets and help you with the bosses but also randomly invade your world to kill you. You'll actually see shadows of other players moving around sometimes or touch a blood stain and see how they died. Really funny and also frightening when you come to an area with many blood stains.
The game plot and history is not forced upon you but revealed in details like the placement of items, corpses and bosses, the item descriptions and selected pieces of dialogue with the mysterious persons you encounter. Excellent game design.
You'll die a lot but you can always train, try a different path, learn to use other weapons and movesets, eventually you'll succeed and it's sweeter than slaying cheap Alduin in Skyrim who falls in a minute thanks to overpowered PC . This game is not only about number crunching though there are a lot of them but about learning your moves and attacks in the first place. A light armor can even be more beneficial imagine that.
TLDR; buy it already while DS1 is a little better DS2 is still great by all usual standards.

Open-world action game as it should be.
has that great feeling of absolute freedom - go anywhere, drive anywhere, fly anywhere! You can get to any place on the huge map in just few seconds, you can be defeated without any penalties - this game is here to entertain you, not to blow your mind or make you angry at your keyboard.
Two unique devices underlying the awesomeness of
are grappling hook and infinitely respawning parachute (infinitely resp...? aw, forget it). Tons of fun guaranteed! Every action game should have it - I really missed them in
. ;-) It brings so much variety and joy in moving and fighting that you'll be travelling for hours here and there just to use them again and again.
The world is really good. Yes, most of the cities and villages are copy-pasted, but there are so many different regions on the map with different climate, weather and views that you'll never get bored. Graphics is on the level too, especially fire and explosions - you'll get addicted to blowing things up! Story and quests are not the strongest part of the game, but they do their job. Another feature worth mentioning is the hidden items' search radar - in my opinion, really great idea. It is finally interesting to find stuff by yourself without spending hours in vain or using guide from the Internet.
There are some cons, of course. Enemies respawning out of nowhere behind your back can be really annoying sometimes. Weapon arsenal is not so big, besides, the lack of ammunition for some weapons leaves you with even less choices. Main story is very short and optional quest lines are not so long either. But there are many things to do on the map - different challenges, races, liquidation contracts... Finally, there's still (and I guess it will be there forever) a bug that prevents you from getting the cherished 100% completion of the game (by the game's internal statistics, not the Steam's one). Thankfully there's only achievement for 75% completion, so no worries, achievement hunters - you'll get your perfect Steam game. ;-)
If you like free roaming in beautiful open-world game, spending time in parachute challenges, races and outpost fightings, searching for hundreds of collectibles and upgrades, spreading chaos by blowing stuff up or just flying around and enjoing you freedom - you'll definitely love
.

Экшн с открытым миром - такой, каким он должен быть.
дарит чувство абсолютной свободы - иди куда хочешь, рули куда хочешь, лети куда заблагорассудится. В любую точку огромной карты можно добраться за секунды, никаких штрафов за гибель героя - эта игра призвана развлекать вас, а не взрывать мозг или доводить до бешенства.
Два уникальных девайса, делающих игру такой шикарной - гарпун и бесконечно восстанавливающийся парашют (бесконечно восстан...? а, неважно). Веселье гарантировано! Эти штуки должны быть в каждом экшене - как мне не доставало их в
!.. ;-) Простое перемещение по миру и заурядные перестрелки становятся настолько разнообразней и веселей, что вы будете путешествовать туда-сюда только для того, чтобы снова воспользоваться ими.
Мир игры по-настоящему хорош. Да, большая часть городков и деревень сделана копи-пастом. Но на карте столько разных мест со своим климатом, погодой, видами вокруг, что скучно не будет. Графика тоже на уровне, особенно огонь и взрывы - вы полюбите разносить всё в щепки! Сюжет и побочные квесты не сильная сторона игры, но своё дело они делают. Отдельного упоминания стоит система поиска скрытых предметов с помощью радара - на мой взгляд, отличное решение! В кои-то веки интересно искать ценные предметы самому, а не бегать часами там, где ничего нет, или сверяться с готовой картой из Инета.
Конечно, есть некоторые минусы. Враги, респавнящиеся из ниоткуда прямо за спиной, порой жутко раздражают. Арсенал не так уж велик, а нехватка патронов для некоторых пушек ещё сильнее ограничивает в выборе. Основная сюжетная линия очень коротка, да и дополнительные квесты проходятся быстро. Тем не менее, заняться есть чем - всяких испытаний, гонок и контрактов на устранение на карте хватает. Наконец, достичь заветного 100%-го прохождения игры (игра ведёт свою внутреннюю статистику, не связаную со Steam) не получится из-за бага, который, очевидно, никто уже не исправит. К счастью, Steam-достижение есть только за 75%-ое прохождение, так что будьте спокойны, охотники за ачивами - вы сможете получить в коллекцию ещё одну "идеальную" игру. ;-)
Если вам нравится рассекать по открытому красивому миру, проводить время за парашютными испытаниями, гонками и сражениями за военные базы, искать сотни спрятанных предметов и апгрейдов, сеять хаос, взрывая всё вокруг, или просто летать, наслаждаясь видом и собственной свободой, вам определённо понравится
.

This game is astonishing. I can't remember the last time in recent years, or if at all, that I've finished a game and been left with such an indescribable feeling.
The voice acting for Sam is absolutely phenomenal, as she reads her diary pages you feel her every emotion, the joy of love and companionship, the trepidation and bewilderment that comes with maturing and finding your place - you accompany her on a journey and that's something that I haven't felt in a game in a long time.
Some of the VA is truly heart-breaking, as we listen to Sam's audio narration we relate to her plight as we have all been there ourselves, we've been the lost teenager that struggles with acceptance, we've been there dealing with that first love, all the highs and the lows. You find yourself sheding tears with her throughout her story, but also sharing in the warmth and happiness that she experiences.
The developers have done a truly fantastic job of creating a house straight out of the 90s, full of pop-culture references and nostalgia inducing items and themes, I found myself completely absorbed by the house and the intimate tale told within.
Something I truly enjoyed were the mixtapes that you find scattered throughout the house that you can listen to in casette players, there's some true Riot Grrrl music in there, solid 90s punk rock that really adds to the intimate 90s feel that is created whilst exploring this house. Heavens To Betsy are especially great, with their track "Complicated" playing over the credits as you complete the game - "I love you so much you could hurt me, so I do it first so you won't see me".
The lack of any "real" or "solid" gameplay may be off-putting for some, there are no enemies, no combat or puzzles - this is a story that unfolds as you journey throughout the house, exploring room to room and learning about it's inhibatants (past and present) and the lives they live.
If you can enter the game with an open mind, and patience to not rush through the game (it is quite short) then you will discover a truly beautiful and stunning narrative that really deserves to be heard.

It's not a game, as such-- there's little in the way of puzzles or obstacles, and no real way to "lose" the game. Rather, it's a storytelling experience, presented in an unusual fashion, and that story is touching, authentic, and greatly enhanced by the game's period atmosphere and immersive visuals. I would highly recommend it.
That said, Gone Home is short-- I finished the story in about three hours-- and has little to no "replay value," so if it looks interesting to you, I would recommend you do what I did-- put it on your Wish List and wait for it to go on sale. $20 is a bit steep for what amounts to a uniquely-presented novella, but if you can get it at half off or thereabouts, it's worth the value.

An interesting exercise in environmental storytelling. Gone Home is a first-person exploration game taking place inside a single abandoned house filled with the memorabialia of its former inhabitants . You pick up objects and examine them for clues as to how to proceed. You'll read through lots of notes, scrapbooks, and other pieces of written material, which will serve as clues/puzzle pieces as well as convey details about the story. Picking up certain objects or entering certain rooms will trigger a voiceover which also explains the story to you. The interface is similar to the Amnesia and Penumbra games, in that you'll use the mouse to pick up and rotate objects, as well as close or open doors, closets, and drawers as you rummage through the house. It's well put together but by the time you get to the end of it you'll really feel like you've wasted your time. The story doesn't develop much, and since you're uncovering snippets of information about something which has happened in the past, there isn't a lot of impact here. You as the player don't have a role in the story - you're a passive observer and there is nothing for you to actually *do* besides trying to figure out what happened.
This game has received a lot of attention, both positive and negative, and a lot has been written about it. At this point it seems like most people are playing it just so that they can feel like they have an informed opinion about it. If you're one of those people who needs to know what "Gone Home" is all about, then sure, go ahead and play it since it's relatively short anyway. For everyone else; don't waste your time. It doesn't work as a game and as a work of art it's shallow and feels insincere.

A wonderful example of a story-driven game. At 2 hours, some might find it lacking. And certainly the regular price is a bit too steep. But I thought it was pretty much a perfect length for what it does. And what it does is unique.
It is a trendsetter: it shows some ways in which gaming can develop as a medium. There's no gunplay nor puzzle-solving. Just an experience of walking around a house and getting to know a family. It plays more like an FPS-style visual novel, or an interactive short story. It's very straightforward. But the story is told in a really great way, and the pay-off is huge.
It is not without its flaws, however. Some of the mechanics are outdated and the System Shock/Half-Life style FPS gameplay feels a bit awkward. The fact that they relish those mechanics makes it worse. Without a fetishistic reliance on the "click at everything to pick it up"-trope, it would've been a better game. Like The Stanley Parable, it It doesn't do anything especially radical to the core FPS or first-person adventure format, but it uses it as the backbone to greatness.
The best thing about Gone Home is not the particular storyline it tells, but the fact that it manages to tell a compelling and coherent story in the course of 90 minutes to 2 hours, while still allowing the player to determine the pace. This creates a unique sense of agency, and intimacy, since the family, and the house, become part of one's experience, and at the end one feels like one has been invited to spend some quality time with a beautiful memory of a slice of life.

If ever a game was proof that quantity does not equal quality, it's Just Cause 2. Don't misunderstand me; Just Cause 2 can be a lot of fun, but the developers seemed to put more effort into creating a huge world than populating it with exciting and varied things to do. The game-world could have a quarter of the size and it wouldn't have much effected the gameplay.
Despite some flaws in the game mechanics (the usual brain-dead AI and stiff controls) the combat was entertaining. Blowing up buildings, numerous weapons and a good selection of vehicles made the fights look like something out of Michael Bay movie. And the graphics are drop-dead gorgeous. But when it came to everything else, the game failed. The plot and characters were terrible, even for an FPS (topped by one of the worst the end-bosses I've seen in years). The sound was unimpressive and - while the terrain rendering was impressive - the building models were ridiculously oversized. But worst was the sheer amount of commuting required to get from one mission to the next; even with the fastest jet there might be as much as ten minutes dead-time as I travel to the start point of the mission. Plus, while some missions were interesting too many devolved into the usual "storm the base" or "drive person to point X while being chased by cops". Furthermore, while much ado has been made of the "grapple", I found it a rather pointless tool hampered by unresponsive controls; it was easier to just shoot the bad-guys.
Just Cause 2 had a number of interesting moments but the title as a whole was marred by a lack of good design and pacing. It takes more than just a huge map to create an entertaining experience.
Lesson learned: Dinosaurs make wars last longer

I'm personally very fond of this game. It's become my most favored first person shooter since CoD: World at War, but I'll try to present a fair review.
This review was written following the release of the "Horrors of War" Expansion for Verdun.
Pros:
-Accurate representation of World War I
-Weapons are fitting to the era and fun!
-You start out with 1914-era uniforms and progress to 1916-era uniforms as you level up with friends.
-Fairly easy to earn medals even if you didn't play all that well.
-The frontlines game-mode really makes you feel like you're participating in the Great War
-The writhing death animations and screams will haunt my dreams for years.
Cons:
-Sometimes your body launches up into the air after being shot. It's kind've funny though.
-The community has been sort've notably infiltrated by the CoD and Battlefield community; you can spot them by their endless whining in the chat.
-Getting good at the game will require you to die at the start of your career. A lot. You'll get better at it with the more time you put into learning the gameplay. Most people tend to give up within the first ten ranks. If you're easily discouraged or prone to breaking blood vessels from high blood pressure, I don't recommend getting this game.
If you're a history buff or have an appreciation for well-made World War games, get it. If you're looking for an "MVG +420 Call of Duty sequel" keep looking.

I just played 7 hours of Warface today after putting a good 200 hours into the closed beta. During the closed beta it was rather good, there weren't a ton of players like there are now and the reason I bring this up is because it factors into my biggest problem with this game that I didn't have back when it was in closed beta:
It is utter and complete♥♥♥♥♥in this game. It makes good players with apparently good connections to the server completely unstoppable killing machines and you'll be looking at him and your teammates like they're all stupid, how could this guy have possibly just slid in on his back like he was launched from a man cannon and kill you and five of your teammates and it's as if no one was reacting to him but you, when in fact, all your teammates probably tried to shoot this fella but it didn't show on your screen, the networking of Warface is so bad it puts Chinese and Russian F2P shooters to shame.
Remember AvA? I do, it was honestly pretty good for PVP and I never had a hit detection issue, it was as solid as CSS and a game that got turned into trash. And now, here we have Warface that suffered from Pay2Win and hackers up the wazoo for the longest time, after Crytek started losing money from no-one playing it, they changed their Pay2Win ways and added FairFight to the game which helps a lot, I see at least five players per match kicked due to FairFight.
Problem is though, the networking is just so bad it seems almost as if a lot of other decent players are cheating because they'll fly in like an eagle on their knees drenched in vaseline and wipe out an entire squad and take no damage as everyone and their mother is firing on this player, he gets up after destroying all of you only to continue his rampage on your unsuspecting teammates who don't pay attention to their mini-map or are apparently deaf to all the gun fire and screaming just ten feet away from them.
Disclaimer:
I remember this game looking pretty good in the closed beta and that's before it was even complete, it was missing a ton of maps, weapons and character customizations that it has now and is still lacking in. Coming from Crytek I was incredibly surprised this looked like an Xbox 360 game when I played it again.
It looks bland and performance is bad, I have a pretty good computer, 4.5GHz FX-4100, 16GB 1333MHz DDR3 RAM, 2GB GDDR5 R9 270 and play on a 24" 1080p monitor. The game constantly randomly hangs up, especially when aiming at players, whether enemies or teammates, it just hangs for a split second and as I'm watching the resources this game is using, it's barely touching any aspect of my system and while I do keep a constant 60FPS, locked with Radeon Settings and not using Vsync I get the same stuttering and hang ups on all settings, from the highest to the lowest, stuttering and hang ups here and there for seemingly no reason. I believe it's caused by the game catching up with the server since it doesn't appear to be my PC's fault and there's no spike in usage.
This is where the game falls flat on it's stupid face. The hit detection is "hit and miss" and there's no pun intended there either, some servers you join you feel unstoppable and your shots hit the second you fire your weapon, but most of the time you'll have to be shooting at someone for about half a second before the game registers you hitting them and a lot of times, even as a sniper, you'll see your shots hit the wall right behind someone standing completely still and then they die once you shoot them a few more times when your shots actually start hitting for some reason. I'm an avid FPS player, like 60% of my 500 Steam games are shooters and 70% of those games are competitive which I play a lot of and I'm rather good at. (2.0 KDR or more in almost every match in almost every game, the only time I do badly is if I'm tired or get terrible spawns.) So believe me when I say this game has hit detection issues. Also, you'll never see anyone with more than maybe two connection bars in a match. I live in sunny California and have my game setup for North America and I've tried every channel. Though that doesn't seem to matter, while changing channels I ended up in the same match I was in previously, all the same players. If you play co-op, you'll notice that your weapons seem to be killing machines all of a sudden and down an enemy in three or so hits and hit instantly, go into PVP and this isn't the case since players are not bots that are operating server side and thus no latency between them and the server like a player. Basically, every few matches or so it'll feel like you're going from COD to Battlefield, COD being that shots instantly hit when fired and Battlefield having bullet drop and bullet delay for added realism. It'll feel like a really terrible version of Battlefield most of the time and then all of a sudden it completely throws you off and it feels like COD, instant hits and only takes a few shots to kill a player and not half a clip or a whole clip depending on how bad it is at times and then the game actually feels really solid when this happens.
Good controls, feels a lot like Battlefield with the control scheme they use, I only changed two or three buttons in the options as the rest were what I'm used to and what I use in most other games. It allows you to customize all controls as well so no complaints there but there is one issue that bugs me. The movement feels very clumsy, I feel as if someone is pulling on my character whenever I move. They're so sluggish it'll probably get you killed. And considering what they're carrying, I'd imagine if they were running for their lives they'd move a lot faster and besides, we can knee slide twenty feet on any surface, even sand and concrete and yet our characters feel like they're bent out of shape, sprinting feels more like a brisk walking pace than a full sprint. Yet, you'll see players online move like the wind. I'm not sure if there's any kind of item that allows you to move faster but I see it all the time. Also, your teammates will push you off from platforms, accidentally or purposely, it'll happen at least every match or they block you and get in your way.

The content in this game is some what lacking, which I don't find a big deal since it's a F2P shooter, there are quite a few maps, co-op levels and more, but it has little to no items in the item shop. Almost no character customization options and most of them are super generic and the only way to get some of them is through crates. There's also a weird unlock system, you choose what kind of equipment you want to unlock when waiting at the lobby screen, depending on your score in the match it unlocks progress in one of three fields of your choosing: Clothing, Weapons or Attachments. You choose one of these three before starting a match and the XP you get in the match towards your rank decides how much percentage you get under your unlock goal.
That's really all I have to say on Warface and I'm fairly disappointed considering it comes from one of my favorite FPS developers, Crytek. I could look past everything else wrong with the game if the hit detection was constant because it is a decent F2P game with decent maps and good ideas. It doesn't bring anything new to the table but it does the whole COD thing fairly well for a F2P game but it's completely ruined by the hit detection.

I'm a bit lost as to what to say about this. Surely, some people might enjoy this interactive museum, but I cannot help but feel like it could never ever be wirth 20 bucks. My recommendation could have been different had the price been as well.
To make it clear - this is a story that can certainly resonate with certain people, however the price makes it not worth too try and find out whether you are one of those people or not.
This is a poor man's Penumbra; the game has 2 primary ways of conveying the plot (for what it's worth - more on that later) - audial diaries and various letters spread about in the house. A diary entry plays in the background each time the player finds the next plot clue, and is then added to the player's library/journal, from where they can play the recording again or read the transcript. Other than that, the house is full of various letters and cards, which can be read if so desired. The content will provide for 2 hours of play time, if explored fully.
The aforementioned house is, by the way, the only location in this game. It's not very large, but has enough dark corners to make the player revisit some rooms; mostly, however, all the clues are pretty straightforward and won't require any particular pixel-hunting.
The environments not very interactive, as the most a player can do is move several small objects (which represent no plot value most of the time) around. With the exclusion of a few exceptions, all interactivity boils down to opening doors, reading letters sticked on surfaces, and turning the lights on. The amount of objects that had any relevant information on them that required examining in 3D can be counted in single digits; for the record - there is an option in this game to rotate some objects in all 3 axis.
The plot mainly consists of one main storyline about a girl (main character's sister). There is also a branch going into the stories of the rest of the family - the writer father, the mother and her colleague♥♥♥♥♥♥ and finally her mysterious brother the pharmacist. There is not much to be gathered all in all, but these branches do provide for a nice distraction from an otherwise monotonous story.
It is hard to comment on the main story itself without going into spoilers (there are not much to be made however). It cannot brag with clever twists or an ability to create a strong emotional bond, even though there were a few unexpected moments. The ending is particularly dissatisfying - it does not solve any problems raised during the game and just reaches an easy deus-ex-machina conclusion, if such strong terms can even be applied in such case.
Speaking of the social commentary side of the plot, there is not much to be either. There is only 1, perhaps two moments where some societal problems are pointed out. That is fair enough - but no further commentary has been made on these topics. Even the reaction of the characters isn't described with more than 2 paragraphs of text.
The graphics are relatively stylised, yet it can still be often seen how poor they are. This game is in many ways comparable to Dear Esther, and the latter has done a much better job at visuals.
It's also worth noting that the game is quite glitchy. I got stck at one point because, despite having a key to the next stage, so to say, I wasn't able to open an appropriate door. I tried restarting the game, only to see the "New Game" button - my save file didn't like my hard drive, apparently. Having turned to the forums, this seemed to have been a pretty widespread issue.
Furthermore, objects sometimes would glitch when picked up, and not be displayed.
Gladly in Gone Home it is easy to reach a previously achieved point in the plot, so even after losing my save file I wasn't set back too far.
All in all, I must say that even thuogh I wasn't bored to the point of quitting the game halfway in, yet that is only due to my having nothing to do at the time. Your time is much better spent playing other games, including indie ones - it is very easy to find a better way to spend your time. If you are interested in such an interactive museum type of game, I suggest you try Dear Esther, which had managed the implementation of it much better. Finally, there is always Bastion with its narration - though that would require more actual gameplay.

Just cause 2 is a Free-roaming Hookshot-em-up that takes the very idea of a freeroamer, builds a game out from that idea, and then multiplies it by a factor of 10^100. It is absolutely brilliant. But if I had to describe the game in 3 words, it would have to be Fun, Amazing and Silly. And anyone who has played a freeroamer knows that a silly game is great. Face up, it seems like your standard freeroamer based around side missions with a main story mixed in. But once you start digging, you never want to stop.
The game has 3 main ideas that the game is buildt upon. Number one: The black market. The black maket is like a vehicle store, a gun shop and a transport system all in one. Here you can buy ammo, if you run out and you're not in a mission, where ammo is free, but you can also buy some vehicles for a bigger price. These are generally one time use only, when you want a fast car, or when an airport is not close enough. It also features a transport system, where it transports you to wherever toy've been before, for free. "Gimmick" number two: The grappling hook. Oh boy, is this thing fun. It seems like your normal grappling hook, only useful to get you from point A to point B, but this thing is so much more useful. Yes, it can just get you from A to B if thats what you want, but it can also drag you to vehicles, such as Helicopters and Cars that are usually really hard to hijack when they are moving, plus that it has the ability to drag people too you, if that is an enemy or just a random NPC that you met on the street. "Gimmick" number three: Chaos. Instead of your usual points system, Just Cause 2 features a Chaos system, that you get my doing missions, destroying enemy property, blowing stuff up, or getting Heat. Heat is a system that shows how agressive the military is against you. If it is at 0, then they wont attack you. At max however, they want you dead at all costs. Instead of a 5 star meter like in GTA, it is a bar, that progressively fills, so you exactly know how much they're after you. When your Chaos meter eventually drops to 0, you get some chaos and some money. Chaos unlocks missions, items in the blakc market, but most importantly, it unlocks story missions. Which is important, since it encourages you to jerk around and have a blast, which is what this game does best. With an absolutely HUGE map, breathtaking visuals, great vehicles and stunning gameplay, this is a game worth buying. At only 15€, it's definately worth picking up. I give Just Cause 2 a 10/10.

Just cause 2 is a Free-roaming Hookshot-em-up that takes the very idea of a freeroamer, builds a game out from that idea, and then multiplies it by a factor of 10^100. It is absolutely brilliant. But if I had to describe the game in 3 words, it would have to be Fun, Amazing and Silly. And anyone who has played a freeroamer knows that a silly game is great. Face up, it seems like your standard freeroamer based around side missions with a main story mixed in. But once you start digging, you never want to stop.
The game has 3 main ideas that the game is buildt upon. Number one: The black market. The black maket is like a vehicle store, a gun shop and a transport system all in one. Here you can buy ammo, if you run out and you're not in a mission, where ammo is free, but you can also buy some vehicles for a bigger price. These are generally one time use only, when you want a fast car, or when an airport is not close enough. It also features a transport system, where it transports you to wherever toy've been before, for free. "Gimmick" number two: The grappling hook. Oh boy, is this thing fun. It seems like your normal grappling hook, only useful to get you from point A to point B, but this thing is so much more useful. Yes, it can just get you from A to B if thats what you want, but it can also drag you to vehicles, such as Helicopters and Cars that are usually really hard to hijack when they are moving, plus that it has the ability to drag people too you, if that is an enemy or just a random NPC that you met on the street. "Gimmick" number three: Chaos. Instead of your usual points system, Just Cause 2 features a Chaos system, that you get my doing missions, destroying enemy property, blowing stuff up, or getting Heat. Heat is a system that shows how agressive the military is against you. If it is at 0, then they wont attack you. At max however, they want you dead at all costs. Instead of a 5 star meter like in GTA, it is a bar, that progressively fills, so you exactly know how much they're after you. When your Chaos meter eventually drops to 0, you get some chaos and some money. Chaos unlocks missions, items in the blakc market, but most importantly, it unlocks story missions. Which is important, since it encourages you to jerk around and have a blast, which is what this game does best. With an absolutely HUGE map, breathtaking visuals, great vehicles and stunning gameplay, this is a game worth buying. At only 15€, it's definately worth picking up. I give Just Cause 2 a 10/10.

Gone home in short is a an story driven empathy game with a focus on exploration.
While I personally didn’t connect with the story, it was none the less interesting and accompanied by beautifully detailed set pieces and an excellent aesthetic it was enjoyable to play through.
Pros:
+ well delivered voice acting
+ 90's nostalgia aesthetic felt polished
+ great texture work and art peices throughout
+ great use of lighting and sound to create tension and a mysterious atmosphere
+ good use of humour
+ short enough to play in one session
Cons:
- hard to justify the $25 AU ($20 US) price tag for this length of game with no replayability
- music tapes felt like they could have been a more interesting mechanic then just some bands music, possibility for more story telling?
- introduces interesting side narratives (family history) but does not elaborate on them before moving on to delving deeper into the main narrative
- teenage girl narrative will not appeal to some male audiences, and feministic undertones mixed in the main narrative could be poorly received (I believe this is why some people are quick to judge Gone Home negatively)
Overall:
6/10
A great game to knock over on a rainy Sunday night when you're looking for a short story.
My partner enjoyed it a lot more then I did, but considering I didn't really feel like the target audience that makes a lot of sense.
I look forward to seeing the empathy story game genre develop from these early steps, and I believe gone home will be remembered as one of the titles that started it off.

I really wanted to like this game. It's hard to argue that the way it tells its story is captivating, and it's very rewarding to piece together the lives of all the characters invovled. If nothing else, it's a promising testimony to the potential of exploration-driven narrative.
So what's the problem?
The story SUCKS. (Spoilers ahead.)
Towards the end of the game, I began to realise that the big 'reveal' was something I had predicted from about half an hour into the game - the black sheep of the family is a lesbian, and has run off to be with her new girlfriend. I can only assume that the developers expected this to elicit some kind of controversial or surprised reaction from the game's audience, but in honesty, I just found it extremely patronising that this kind of thing can still be considered a 'plot twist'. Is the daughter coming out as gay really significant enough to be the crux of an entire plot-driven game? Perhaps a decade or two ago.
Sure, it was a nice story of a troubled young teenage girl discovering her own identity, and in a way, it was very sweet. However, the story is initially presented as something far more shocking - answerphone messages at the beginning of the game had me prepared for an out and out revenge-slasher plotline, or at least something with a little more drama. The real kicker is that the very real sense of mystery and looming dread that pervades the game all feels pointless in the end.
The house as a storytelling device was a stroke of genius, and really, it's very well executed. It's just a shame they didn't fill it with a story worth a damn.

The Good:
* Creepy atmosphere drives your intrigue
* Letters, music and scenery set the mid 90's period perfectly
* Audio journal is superbly written and narrated
* Subtle jokes and nods that really work
* Some clever, if subtle, misdirection in the plotting
* Keeps you guessing and exploring
* Lots to read and doled out in clever natural ways
The Bad: (nitpicking)
* Short? 2 hours is enough time to complete
* Little to no replay value (possibly a Commentary play-through)
* A couple of lock combinations are easy to miss
* Would have like more problem solving
* Secrets are findable at any time and technically you can end the game in under 60secs
* Some odd frame rate issues for no apparent reason
Background: Heard good things, had to try it out.
Impressions: Wow, what a great ride. Very impressed by the writing and execution that played out perfectly as I explored and all made logical sense while apparently giving you semi-open world freedom it's actually guiding you. there are easter eggs in almost every location if you look for them and none are necessary or over explained you just have to be observant. Nothing jarred me out of the game and finding a cereal box with the puzzle completed on the side in pen just shows the level of detail that goes into making this house feel lived in.
Be aware this is an interactive story and 2 hours is all it takes to complete. There are adult themes that are handled cleverly and that reading and thought is needed to get the most out of the experience as the game allows you to join the dots yourself for the broad themes and side stories.
Recommended for: 90's music lovers, those with a literary passion and point n click explorers.
Conclusion: 7/10. A pitch perfect story, expertly delivered in every way but beware the length and how much you want to pay.

I have no problem with games defined as "walking simulators". The Stanley Parable was funny and very enjoyable, as was Jazzpunk, Fract OSC has a great music element, Naissancee had some great platforming and interesting exploration, and Kairo had some cool, minimalistic puzzles. Correction, I like walking simulators if there's something to do in the game.
There is nothing to do in Gone Home. Going into this game, I expected a ♥♥♥♥ing masterpiece the way the review scores were mapped out. Every reviewer was basically giving this unlimited amounts of praise. Turns out that this was a poorly written short story disguised as a "game."
In Gone Home, you play as a person who goes home to see their family, but realizes no one is home. You go inside and walk around, to try to find journals to piece together a "story". The game takes around an hour to finish and it will be a thoroughly unenjoyable one. First of all, there really is no gameplay. If holding the W key and clicking the Left Mouse Button often is called gameplay to you, then you'll have a fun time. I appreciate the design, but if you're making a short story, MAKE A ♥♥♥♥ING SHORT STORY. If I pay money for a game, I'm paying money for a game. Don't give me this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t about how it is an experience, or something like that. This is supposed to be a game. I expect a game. The other only thing that the game really has is story. And boy, they couldn't even do that right.
If people tell you the story is engaging, they are certainly lying to you. The story is something I person cannot relate with , and I doubt 90% of people will be able to either. It also doesn't help that this is the most cliched story ever. You'll probably be able to guess the ending halfway through the game, and if you can't, you haven't read enough sappy love tales. This game probably would have been better IF they made a good story. If a walking simulator has a fascinating story, then I will be able to enjoy it. Unfortunately this falls in the same category as garbage video games like Dear Esther, which have the worst of both worlds when it comes to gameplay and story. I'm sick of people saying that this game is amazing, because this isn't even a game. This is an interactive story, that sounds like it was written by a Grade 6 child who was forced to write a story about life experiences or something like that.
If you were even thinking about purchasing this game, turn away and buy something else. Luckily I had this in a bundle, but please don't drop 20 bucks, or 5 bucks even for this game. If you search up "Lesbian Love Story" online, you'll find thousands of stories better than this. This is an insult to gaming and gamers alike.

Five Nights at Freddy's 2 is the terrifying sequel to the enourmously popular indie horror game, Five Nights at Freddy's. Like the original, you work the night shift in a local pizzaria and are being hunted down by spooky animatronics.
FNaF 2 is similar in gameplay to the first game, but it also changes quite a few things. I like that about it. For example, the number of evil animatronics has increased from 4 to 10. There are now 3 ways that the animatronics can enter your office and jumpscare you instead of 2. There are also no doors. Thanks, Scott.
The game's scares will mainly happen through jumpscares, but the atmospheric music and noise is very good at creating tension and dread. You now work in a larger building. You have a flashlight that you can shine in the hallway and in various rooms. Instead of the whole building running out of power when you use up to much energy, only the flashlight will die. This, however, can be as fatal as the pitch darkness experienced in FNaF, because you must shine your light down the hall to survive. This brings me to another topic.
You will die. A lot. I highly discourage purchasing this game before playing the original. This game is DIFFICULT. It took me 3 hours to complete nights 1-5.  (Remember, nights last roughly 8 minutes and 30 seconds.) This isn't a game you can just play and beat easily. You will have to do research on the behavior of all 10 animatronics before you can even have hopes of getting past night 3. However, this leads to an amazing feeling of acheivement whenever you pass the night.
There is a very interesting and creepy backstory to FNaF, and many parts of the sequel shed light on the events such as "The Bite of '87" and the missing children. The community is always coming up with new explanations and theories, and they are all interesting.
But is the actual game scary? The answer to this question both yes, and no. The animatronics definitely are terrifying. The new designs of the old ones-- Freddy, Bonnie, Chica, and Foxy-- are partly destroyed, and it looks scary. The new "toy" animatronics are creepy. But it lost something that the old FNaF had. The dread of not being able to find a certain animatronic. There are too many to keep track of to really think about the terrifying situation you're in, and whenever you see one, whether it be in the vents or in the hallway, there's always an easy way to get rid of it, if you've done the proper research. (I should add that "proper research" is neccesary, if you want to survive.) It takes away the suspense, and the mystery a horror game should have. By night 3, I can admit that nothing that happened really scared me. Startled me when a jumpscare occured, sure.♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥me off when Balloon Boy came in my room and turned off my means of defense, definitely. But scared me? No.
This doesn't mean FNaF 2 is a bad game. In fact, it's really fun to take turns playing it at a party and watching people yell as the animatronics kill them is funny and entertaining. But it doesn't offer the suspense of other horror games and the original FNaF.
This is what my verdict is: Play the first game. If you really want more, get the second. It offers more difficulty and crazy jumpscares than the original, but keep in mind that it definitely is not the scariest horror game you'll play.

Alright, so let me start off by saying this:
As a Souls game, it's not good. It's just not. I remember finishing this a couple of days after release on 360 and then selling it. I hated it at the time, and went right back to Dark Souls 1 happily.
But Scholar of the First Sin fixed quite a few things, and I'm starting to gain an appreciation for it. The game definitely looks better, runs better, a lot of glitches were fixed.
The pros:
Connectivity is a lot better. Summoning someone in DaS 1 was HELL. Now it's nowhere near as bad. You'll encounter some issues sometimes, but it's nothing that can't be fixed quickly.
Armor/weapon variety. This is one of the best things about the game, and it definitely trumps over 1's armor/weapon variety.
A few other minor things like you can use souls such as 'soul of a nameless soldier' all at once instead of 1 by 1.
The DLC areas are the best part about the game. Hands down.
Cons:
Soul memory.
Adaptability.
Weapon move sets feel copied and pasted sometimes and aren't as unique.
Some enemies act like they're on a swivel chair. ESPECIALLY the salamanders.
The PvP feels awful and floaty. I get hit when I clearly did not. This happens in Dark Souls 1, but that's because of major latency issues between the 2 players. Here, it happens all. the. time. The netcode is god awful, but because of the weapon/armor variety I have a love/hate relationship with it.
That's all I can really think of. Overall, I think it's worth a playthrough, and you can be the judge of PvP. I got fun out of the single player.
